problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14065925/assets/701c883ef9f721f9dad8fb59236fbbd297cfac3d3d8845a18d3493d788f8d8a8.png)

Paint is leaking from a tank and is forming a circle on the floor. If the area of the circle is increasing at the rate of $12\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{2}/\text{min}$, how fast is the circumference of the circle increasing at the moment when the radius is $4\,\text{mm}?$
worked_solution:
In this situation, we want to find $\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}$ at the moment when $r=4,$ and we are also told that  $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=12\pi .$

To start, let's set up an equation relating the area $A$ and the circumference $C$ of the circle. Since $C=2\pi r$ and $A=\pi {r}^{2},$ the relationship between $A$ and $C$ is

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2}=\pi {(\frac{C}{2\pi })}^{2}=\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}C}(\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{C}{2\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

When $r=4\,\text{mm},$ $C=2\pi (4)=8\pi \text{ mm}.$ Hence, substituting $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=12\pi $ and $C=8\pi $, and solving for $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}12\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{8\pi }{2\pi } \\ 12\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}\cdot 4 \\ \frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{12\pi }{4} \\ \frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t} & =3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the circumference is increasing at a rate of $3\pi \text{ mm/min}.$

Question 10
?

Paint is leaking from a tank and is forming a circle on the floor. If the area of the circle is increasing at the rate of 12πmm2/min, how fast is the circumference of the circle increasing at the moment when the radius is 4mm?

a
3πmm/min
b
4πmm/min
c
1.5mm/min
d
3mm/min
e
2πmm/min
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this situation, we want to find dCdt at the moment when r=4, and we are also told that dAdt=12π.

To start, let's set up an equation relating the area A and the circumference C of the circle. Since C=2πr and A=πr2, the relationship between A and C is

A=πr2=π(C2π)2=C24π.

Differentiating this relationship with respect to t using implicit differentiation, we get

ddt(A)=ddt(C24π)dAdt=dCdt⋅ddC(C24π)dAdt=dCdt⋅C2π.

When r=4mm, C=2π(4)=8π mm. Hence, substituting dAdt=12π and C=8π, and solving for dAdt. We get

12π=dCdt⋅8π2π12π=dCdt⋅4dCdt=12π4dCdt=3π.

We conclude that the circumference is increasing at a rate of 3π mm/min.
